subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 35-year-old man of sub-Saharan African ancestry has had several episodes of jaundice and dark urine after taking sulfa drugs; between episodes his hemoglobin is normal. His maternal uncle has had similar episodes, and his father has never had jaundice.
question: Which of the following best describes the inheritance of this condition?
explanation_correct: G6PD deficiency is an X-linked recessive disorder and is the most common human enzyme deficiency. It is most prevalent in populations from malaria-endemic regions because heterozygosity confers protection against Plasmodium falciparum, and male relatives on the maternal side are typically affected.

explanation_incorrect.B: Autosomal recessive inheritance would require an affected sibling or consanguinity and would not explain the sex-specific pattern seen in this family.
explanation_incorrect.C: Autosomal dominant inheritance would produce affected individuals in every generation with an affected parent, which is not the case here.
explanation_incorrect.D: X-linked dominant inheritance would affect daughters of an affected father and would not spare the father while affecting a maternal uncle.
explanation_incorrect.E: Mitochondrial inheritance is transmitted only through the mother and would affect both sexes equally with variable severity, unlike this enzyme deficiency.

educationalObjective: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern.
